title: Autopsy report complete on teen who died in police custody
subtitle: Family says conclusion Wilfred Asham died of probable heart problem not good enough
article: The family of Wilfred Asham, who died in police custody in September, isn't satisfied with a newly released autopsy report that says the 19-year-old died of a probable heart arrhythmia.
Medical investigators have told the family that heart arrhythmia can't be proven, family members said Tuesday.
"We were expecting something more definitive, something more specific, something you could put your finger on and say, 'That is the cause of death,'" says the family's lawyer, David Soper.
"Not getting answers is what's hard," says Asham's mother, Sheila McKenzie.
Toxicology tests showed Asham had some traces of marijuana in his system and his blood-alcohol level was 0.12, above the legal limit. However, medical investigators said that did not kill him.

His family says the autopsy report does not explain changes they saw to his face after he had died, including, they say, bruising, redness and a previously broken nose that appeared to have been straightened.
"We can't go on what that report said, because it's not right," says McKenzie."We know, we've seen his face. We know there's trauma to his face. But the autopsy says there was no trauma."
The family is willing to exhume Asham's body for an independent autopsy.
"We don't have the money for an independent autopsy, but we feel under these circumstances, the state should pay for an independent autopsy," says Asham's stepfather, Lou Vosters.
Asham, was arrested around 12:30 a.m. CTonSept. 2during an investigation into a stolen vehicle in the Weston area of Winnipeg.
Moments after placing Asham in a holding room at the Public Safety Building, police said they realized he was not breathing. CPR was administered and Asham was rushed to hospital, where he died.

Asham's family had hoped for the chance to review videotapes of their son's last moments in police custody. But although some rooms at the Public Safety Building are equipped with cameras, the room where Asham was held does not have one, police say.
"We want cameras in all those rooms, so that whenever somebody goes in one of those rooms, people are going to know that no foul play happened," McKenzie said Tuesday.
Police refused to comment on the situation until their investigation into the death is complete, which is expected in a couple of weeks.
